_about: Shared walk vectors for CIE graph format version 6 (docs/event-collection/cie-v6-binary.md section 6).  Each case: a graph, the game, the random stream (each roll taken % n; none for n <= 1), the villagers bound, the answer clicked at each question (its choice index), the run-time facts (null = every bound villager harmable, every threshold met) and whether the Unicode Text companion is on.  expect: the path, each effect's roll [a, b], each pool pick [pool, instance, item index] in draw order, the aliases drawn, each popup's text as the player reads it (before paging), the rolls used and the compiled .cieg's SHA-256.  Run by tests/test_cie_graph_v6.py and the engine's emulator tests.

collection.credit: Test fixture: the design's worked example (A6).

items: neat rows with carefully labeled plants
a winding garden with shaded places to sit
hardy food plants that require little attention
flowers chosen to attract helpful insects
a mixture of familiar plants and experimental varieties
a traditional layout remembered by the elders
The village gains a peaceful place to gather and learn.
The elder rests on a bench, pleased that the younger villagers listened without copying the past blindly.
A child presents both gardeners with a leaf labeled "BEST."
A nursing parent enjoys the shade while talking with friends; the infant is never assigned a gardening task.
The gardeners agree to compare notes again after the next harvest.

intro.name: Two plans
intro.text:
Two skilled gardeners have developed different plans for a small community garden near the village. (Gardener1) favors {A.1}, while (gardener2) favors {A.2}.
An elder says that both plans have merit. A child asks whether there will be room to play. A nursing mother nearby suggests a place where parents can sit with their babies while older children explore safely.

choices.label: Combine the best features into one shared garden.
Give each gardener a small plot to demonstrate the plan.

s1.text: The gardeners cooperate, creating a beautiful and useful space.

s2.text: They argue over the path's exact shape, then compromise when the elder suggests a curved path with straight planting beds.

s3.text: A child draws an elaborate map featuring a "secret frog kingdom." The gardeners reserve a small corner for wildlife.

s4.text: The gardeners realize that the combined plan needs more work than they can manage. They simplify it rather than overpromise.

p1.text: Both gardens flourish in different ways. The villagers learn which designs suit which purposes.

p2.text: One garden produces more food, while the other becomes a favorite resting place. Neither is declared a failure.

p3.text: The gardeners become playful rivals and begin leaving compliments disguised as criticisms.

p4.text: A plant grows across the dividing line. The gardeners spend an absurd amount of time deciding who owns it.
